summary: Iteration 7 full-stack test: oven_type field (backend + Gestione forno UI), quantity-aware mixer/forming scheduling in 'Quando impastare' (StartDoughs) incl. the user's 5000-buns vs 19-loaves example, weekly-plan -> sd-load-day quantity link, and regression of Quando infornare, weekly plan, oven timers, announcements CRUD, photo diagnosis, AI chat markdown, IT/DE language switch+persist. Backend: 64/64 pytest passing. Frontend: all tested flows working, no console errors.

ui_bugs.issue: Numeric pieces input is too narrow: a value of 5000 renders visually clipped as '500' (value is correct, only display is truncated). Now that 4-5 digit batch quantities are a core use case (5000 hamburger buns), widen the field or reduce font size.

issues: No warning when 'attesa' is very large (measured 329 min wait for the 19-piece dough while the 5000-piece batch occupies the forming station) — schedule is mathematically correct but a dough waiting >5h after its rest will over-proof; consider a visual warning/threshold or splitting large batches.

action_items: Widen weekly-pieces-{id} input so 4-5 digit quantities are fully visible
Optional: dedicated i18n key for the 'no rows' toast in StartDoughs (currently reuses weekly_empty_share) and an over-proofing warning when attesa exceeds a threshold
critical_code_review_comments: StartDoughs.compute(): forming station uses FIFO by readyToForm; it does not consider that a long forming job can force a later dough to over-proof. If that matters for the bakery, order forming by (readyToForm, formMin) or warn.
StartDoughs loadDay() hardcodes mix_min=15 and sec_piece=4 for plan-loaded rows; consider persisting these per recipe so the plan link is fully data-driven.
Mixer order sort on rest_min uses Number() on string inputs — correct, but equal-rest ties depend on row order; deterministic secondary key (e.g. formMin desc) would make output stable.
